- Confidence: low - there are no measured counts, and my knowledge ends in June 2026.
- What would change it: Running c1-c4 in the drill-down, which would replace the qualitative impressions with counts.

## What the data shows
I have no measured data for volume, window, tone, source concentration or place coverage. I cannot give a sourced value for any of these facets.

- **Tariffs and pricing.** Mobile tariff hikes in July 2024 were widely covered (est.).
- **5G and fixed wireless.** Rollout of 5G and JioAirFiber was a recurring subject (est.).
- **Jio Platforms listing.** Reports on a planned IPO (est.).
- **Streaming.** The JioCinema and Disney Star merger, which led to JioHotstar (est.).
- **Regulation and competition.** Disputes with Airtel and Vodafone Idea over spectrum, TRAI and satellite spectrum allocation (est.).
- **Group finance.** Jio Financial Services and Reliance Industries results (est.).

- Mukesh Ambani (chair).
- Akash Ambani (chair of Jio Platforms).
- Isha Ambani.
- Sunil Mittal (Airtel rival).
- Telecom regulators and ministers.

Organisations (est.):
- Bharti Airtel
- Vodafone Idea
- TRAI
- Disney
- Meta and Google (Jio Platforms investors, 2020)

I cannot produce a monthly series. A chart with invented points would be unsourced, so I have included none. Any direction claim (rising or falling) is unmeasured.

## Comparison
No baseline corpus was queried, so I cannot state tone against the corpus baseline. The comparison needs news.compare with Jio against Airtel and Vodafone Idea on one scale (share of articles, with the baseline defined as all Indian telecom coverage in the same window).

## Geography (optional)
I cannot state a placed_pct or any place ranking. Many articles carry no place, so a future place share would only describe the placed subset.

- Decision: Treat the Jio IPO, tariffs and AI/datacentre plans as the live narratives to monitor. Do not read the high "critical" share as hostile tone.
- Confidence: medium - the counts are large (12,858 articles) [c1], but the data ends 2026-05-31, and entity labels are machine-assigned and unverified.
- What would change it: A refresh past May 2026, or article-level checks showing the labels or the critical flag are mis-assigned.

## What the data shows
- **Volume:** 12,858 articles mention "reliance jio" between 2024-06-01 and 2026-05-31 (mention match mode) [c1]. 7,969 of them (62.0%) are flagged critical [c1]. That share is computed from [c1] counts: 7,969 / 12,858.
- **Direction:** Volume is falling. Monthly counts went from 605 in June 2024 to 396 in May 2026 [c1], with a peak of 890 in March 2025 [c1]. The late third is 0.66 of the early third, a CAGR of -19.9% [c1].
- **Tone:** 79.9% of articles are positive and 18.3% negative [c1]. The negative-to-positive ratio is 0.23, against a corpus baseline of 0.58, or 0.4 times the baseline [c1]. The coverage is markedly more positive than ordinary news.
- **Critical flag vs. sentiment:** "Critical" (62.0%) [c1] and "negative" (18.3%) [c1] are different measures. Many critical articles are positive in polarity. Examples are the AI-investment piece (Register, 2026-02-20) and the patents piece (TelecomTalk, 2026-05-30) [c1]. I read "critical" as a priority/scrutiny flag, not an attack. This is interpretation.
- **Themes (categories):** business 29.1%, technology 28.5%, telecommunications 19.7% (lift 129.7), finance 8.3% [c1].
- **Themes (subcategories):** prepaid plans 1,046 articles (10.9%), IPOs 528 (5.5%), 5G infrastructure 463 (4.8%), IPOs and listings 341 (3.6%), satellite communication systems 182 (1.9%), M&A 224 (2.3%) [c1].
